title: Mysteries hidden from prophets and angels made known to her

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 11, cols. C-D (PDF p. 35)

source_text: Nosti o Maria, quae Patriarchas et prophetas latebant. Didicisti, o Virgo, quae adhuc Angelis etiam fuerunt abscondita. Audisti, o sanctissima, quae nunquam, divino spiritu afflatorum chorus audire meruit. Moyses et David, Esaias ac Daniel, cunctique prophetae de ipso praedicaverunt: sed modum rationemve ignorarunt. Tu vero sola, o sanctissima Virgo, quae his omnibus ignota fuerunt mysteria, nunc suscipis, causamque intelligis. Nam ubi Spiritus Sanctus, cuncta prompte atque incunctanter perficiuntur. Ubi divina adest gratia, omnia Deo sunt possibilia.
pass_a_gloss: You know (nosti), O Mary, the things which lay hidden from (latebant) the Patriarchs and prophets. You have learned (didicisti), O Virgin, things which until now were hidden (abscondita) even from the Angels. You have heard (audisti), O most holy one, things which never the choir of those breathed upon by the divine spirit (divino spiritu afflati) deserved (meruit) to hear. Moses and David, Isaiah and Daniel, and all the prophets preached/foretold (praedicaverunt) about Him: but the manner or reason (modum rationemve) they did not know (ignorarunt). You truly alone, O most holy Virgin, the mysteries (mysteria) which were unknown (ignota) to all these, now receive (suscipis), and understand (intelligis) the cause (causa). For where the Holy Spirit is, all things readily (prompte) and without hesitation (incunctanter) are accomplished (perficiuntur). Where divine grace is present (adest), all things are possible (possibilia) to God.

choices.choice: 'omnia Deo sunt possibilia': the wording matches Matthew 19:26 / Mark 10:27, while the Annunciation context points to the angel's word in Luke 1:37; both cited inline, Mark 10:27 left in this note.

choices.issue: Quae adhuc Angelis etiam fuerunt abscondita
choices.choice: 'Quae adhuc Angelis etiam fuerunt abscondita' may recall 1 Peter 1:12 or Ephesians 3:9-10; uncertain, not cited.
'divino spiritu afflatorum chorus' rendered 'the choir of those inspired by the divine Spirit' (the inspired prophets;
'divino spiritu' kept, capitalised because it is the Spirit of God).
Margin variant 'al. suscipe et intellige' (imperatives: 'receive and understand') not adopted; the print's indicatives fit 'nunc' and the run of the passage.

pass_b_english: You know, Mary, what was hidden from the patriarchs and prophets. You have learned, O Virgin, what until now was hidden even from the angels. You have heard, most holy one, what the choir of those inspired by the divine Spirit was never found worthy to hear. Moses and David, Isaiah and Daniel, and all the prophets foretold Him, but they did not know the manner or the reason. But you alone, most holy Virgin, now receive the mysteries that were unknown to all of them, and you understand their cause. For where the Holy Spirit is, all things are brought to completion readily and without delay. Where divine grace is present, all things are possible with God (Luke 1:37; Matthew 19:26).
notes: 'omnia Deo sunt possibilia': the wording matches Matthew 19:26 / Mark 10:27, while the Annunciation context points to the angel's word in Luke 1:37; both cited inline, Mark 10:27 left in this note. 'Quae adhuc Angelis etiam fuerunt abscondita' may recall 1 Peter 1:12 or Ephesians 3:9-10; uncertain, not cited. 'divino spiritu afflatorum chorus' rendered 'the choir of those inspired by the divine Spirit' (the inspired prophets; 'divino spiritu' kept, capitalised because it is the Spirit of God). Margin variant 'al. suscipe et intellige' (imperatives: 'receive and understand') not adopted; the print's indicatives fit 'nunc' and the run of the passage.
